ORDER:

He is prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 269, 270,
271, 272 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code (for short '1.P.C.') and under Sections 58, 59 and 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act (for short FSS Act').
4.

Sri N.A. Ramachandra Murthy, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the issue involved in this criminal petition stands on the same footing as that of Criminal Petition No.3731 of 2018 and batch; Criminal Petition No.5421 of 2019 and batch; and Criminal Petition No.5103 of 2019 and batch and requested to pass similar order.
The same is not disputed by the learned Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondents.

5. This Court in Criminal Petition No.3731 of 2019 and batch; Criminal Petition No.5421 of 2019 and batch; and Criminal Petition No.5103 of 2019 and batch has quashed the criminal proceedings launched against various persons by holding that the prosecution under the aforesaid Sections of law To, wh PR in the facts and circumstances of the case is not maintainable under law.

Therefore,
the petitioner herein, who is also similarly placed and is facing the prosecution for the Same nature of offences, is also entitled to the similar relief.
